name: Statistics for Data Science
certifications: No single required certification; assessed by analysis notebooks and a written report
Optional: SAS Certified Statistical Business Analyst
tools: Python with pandas, SciPy and statsmodels

beginner.summary: For analysts, aspiring data scientists and engineers who need statistics they can use on real data. Covers types of data, descriptive statistics, visualising distributions, probability, conditional probability and Bayes' theorem, random variables, common distributions, sampling and the central limit theorem, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, t-tests, chi-square tests, ANOVA, correlation, simple and multiple regression and communicating results, with every topic practised in Python notebooks on business data.
prerequisites: Works with or wants to work with data
outcomes: Describe and visualise data and choose the right summary for its type
Use probability, distributions and sampling to reason about uncertainty
Run and interpret confidence intervals, t-tests, chi-square tests, ANOVA and regression in Python
Explain statistical results and their limits to non-statisticians

days.topic: Statistics for Data Science Overview and Tool Setup
subtopics: What statistics adds to data science and analytics
Uncertainty and why single numbers mislead
Installing Python, Jupyter and the course libraries
pandas for loading and inspecting data
SciPy and statsmodels for statistical methods
R as an alternative and when teams use it
The course datasets: sales, customers, web traffic and operations
days.lab_task: Set up a Python environment with Jupyter and the course libraries, load the sales dataset, list three business questions it could answer and classify each as descriptive, inferential or predictive.
days.deliverable: Working notebook environment and a classified question list
checks: The notebook imports pandas, SciPy and statsmodels without errors
Rows, columns and data types of the sales dataset are reported
Each question is labelled descriptive, inferential or predictive with a reason
objectives: Explain the role of statistics in data science

days.topic: Types of Data and Variables
days.lab_task: Build a data dictionary for the customer dataset that classifies every column by type and scale, fixes wrongly typed columns in pandas and names the right summary for each variable.
days.deliverable: Data dictionary and a type-corrected dataset
checks: Every column has a type and a measurement scale
Identifier and date columns are stored with the right types
Each variable has a suitable summary statistic

days.topic: Descriptive Statistics: Centre and Spread
subtopics: When the median is better than the mean
days.lab_task: Summarise order values overall and by region with centre and spread measures, explain where the mean and median differ and why, and compute a weighted average price.
checks: Centre and spread are reported overall and by region
Mean and median differences are explained with the data
The weighted average matches a manual calculation
objectives: Summarise data with centre and spread

days.topic: Visualising Distributions: Histograms, Box Plots and Density Plots
subtopics: Why the shape of data matters
Skewness and kurtosis in plain terms
days.lab_task: Plot order values with histograms at three bin widths, box plots by region and a log-scale density plot, and describe the shape, skew and outliers in plain words.
checks: All three chart types are produced
Skew and outliers are described correctly
Regional differences are visible and explained

days.topic: Probability Rules and Counting
days.lab_task: Answer eight probability questions about customer orders and defects by formula, then check each answer with a simulation of one hundred thousand trials.
checks: Simulated probabilities agree with the formulas
Independent and mutually exclusive cases are told apart correctly

days.topic: Conditional Probability and Bayes' Theorem
subtopics: The multiplication rule for dependent events
Medical test and fraud alert examples
days.lab_task: Build a contingency table of fraud alerts and confirmed fraud, calculate the chance that an alert is real with Bayes' theorem and show how the answer changes with the base rate.
checks: The contingency table totals match the data
The probability that an alert is real is calculated correctly
The effect of three base rates is explained

days.topic: Random Variables, Expectation and Variance
subtopics: Random variables as numbers from chance events
Variance and standard deviation of a random variable
days.lab_task: Model daily returns of a product as a discrete random variable, compute its expected value and variance by hand and by simulation, and use expected value to compare two promotion options.
days.deliverable: Random variable model and promotion comparison
checks: Expected value and variance match by hand and by simulation
The sum of two days is computed with the rules for sums
The promotion choice uses expected value and its spread

days.topic: Discrete Distributions: Binomial and Poisson
subtopics: Means and variances of each distribution
Poisson as an approximation to the binomial
Fitting counts to a Poisson model
days.lab_task: Model conversions per hundred visitors with a binomial distribution and support tickets per hour with a Poisson distribution, calculate tail probabilities and check the fit against observed counts.
days.deliverable: Two distribution models with fit checks
checks: Each process is matched to the right distribution with reasons
Tail probabilities are computed with SciPy
Observed and expected counts are compared

days.topic: The Normal Distribution and Z-Scores
days.lab_task: Standardise delivery times, find the share of late deliveries with the normal model, check normality with a Q-Q plot and test whether a log transform improves the fit.
days.deliverable: Normal model analysis with fit checks
checks: Late delivery shares are calculated from the normal model
The Q-Q plot shows whether the transform helps

days.topic: Sampling Distributions, Standard Error and the Central Limit Theorem
days.lab_task: Draw repeated samples of different sizes from a skewed population, plot the sampling distribution of the mean and show how the standard error shrinks with sample size.
checks: Sampling distributions are plotted for three sample sizes
The sample mean distribution becomes nearly normal as size grows
Standard error changes are explained with numbers

days.topic: Confidence Intervals for Means and Proportions
subtopics: Intervals for a mean with the t distribution
Sample size for a target width
days.lab_task: Calculate 95 percent confidence intervals for average basket size and conversion rate, compare two regions with an interval for the difference and write the result in plain words.
days.deliverable: Confidence interval analysis and plain-language summary
checks: The interval for the regional difference is reported
The summary avoids the common misinterpretation

days.topic: Hypothesis Testing: Null, Alternative, p-Values and Errors
subtopics: p-values and what they are not
Type I and type II errors
days.lab_task: Write null and alternative hypotheses for four business questions, run a test for each, interpret the p-values and judge whether each result matters in practice.
checks: Each question has correct null and alternative hypotheses
p-values are interpreted without common errors
Practical significance is assessed with effect sizes

days.topic: t-Tests for One and Two Samples
days.lab_task: Test whether a new checkout page changed average order value with Welch's t-test, test before-and-after times for the same stores with a paired test and report effect sizes.
days.deliverable: Two t-test analyses with effect sizes
checks: The right t-test is chosen for each design
Test statistics and p-values are correct
Results include effect sizes and intervals

days.topic: Chi-Square Tests for Categorical Data
days.lab_task: Test whether payment method depends on customer segment with a chi-square test, check expected counts, measure the effect size and find which cells drive the result.
checks: The test statistic and p-value are correct
Expected counts are checked and Fisher's test is used where needed
The cells driving the result are named

days.topic: One-Way ANOVA
days.lab_task: Compare average delivery times across four warehouses with ANOVA, check assumptions, run Tukey's test to find which pairs differ and report the effect size.
checks: The report includes effect size and assumption checks

days.topic: Correlation and Covariance
days.lab_task: Build a correlation matrix for marketing spend and sales variables, compare Pearson and Spearman results, show how one outlier changes a correlation and list two spurious correlations.
checks: Pearson and Spearman correlations are reported
Causal claims are avoided with reasons

days.topic: Simple Linear Regression
days.lab_task: Fit a regression of sales on advertising spend, interpret the slope in money terms, plot residuals and give a prediction interval for next month's planned spend.
days.deliverable: Fitted model with interpretation and prediction
checks: The coefficients match the statsmodels output
The slope is explained in business units
A prediction interval is given for planned spend

days.topic: Multiple Linear Regression in Practice
days.lab_task: Model house prices with size, location and age, include a categorical location variable and one interaction, compare two models and report the preferred one.
days.deliverable: Two regression models with a comparison
checks: Both models are fitted with the formula API
Coefficients are interpreted holding other variables fixed
The preferred model is chosen with stated reasons

days.topic: Communicating Statistical Results to Non-Statisticians
subtopics: Charts with intervals and error bars
days.lab_task: Turn one of the course analyses into a one-page summary for a manager with the answer first, an interval chart, the effect in money terms and the main limits.
checks: The first sentence states the finding
The chart shows intervals and is labelled clearly
Assumptions and limits are written in plain words

days.topic: Beginner Capstone: Statistical Analysis of a Business Dataset
days.lab_task: Analyse a retail dataset from questions to answers: describe and visualise it, test two hypotheses, estimate intervals, fit a regression and present a one-page report with recommendations.
checks: Descriptive, inferential and regression parts are complete
Each result is interpreted with effect sizes

intermediate.summary: For analysts and data scientists who know the core tests and need the methods used in real projects. Covers designing experiments and A/B tests, power and sample size, multiple comparisons, nonparametric tests, regression diagnostics, logistic regression, generalised linear models, regularised regression, model selection and cross-validation, bootstrap and permutation methods, Bayesian inference, time series and forecasting, survival analysis, dimensionality reduction, missing data, causal thinking with observational data and statistics for evaluating machine learning models.
prerequisites: Runs t-tests, chi-square tests and regression in Python or R
Understands sampling, confidence intervals and p-values
Works on analysis or modelling projects
outcomes: Design and analyse experiments with correct power and error control
Fit and check regression, logistic and count models and choose between them
Use resampling, Bayesian methods, time series and survival analysis where they fit
Evaluate machine learning models with sound statistics and handle missing data and confounding

days.topic: Designing Experiments and A/B Tests
subtopics: Units of randomisation: users, sessions and stores
days.lab_task: Write an experiment plan for a new pricing page with randomisation unit, metrics and analysis plan, then analyse a simulated result including a sample ratio mismatch check.
checks: The plan states unit, metrics, duration and analysis before results
The sample ratio mismatch check is run and reported
The primary metric result is reported with an interval

days.topic: Statistical Power and Sample Size
subtopics: Sample size for means and proportions
Power for paired and clustered designs
days.lab_task: Calculate sample sizes for detecting a two percent conversion lift and a five percent change in order value, confirm one with simulation and show what an underpowered test would report.
checks: Simulated power agrees with the formula
The risks of an underpowered test are shown with numbers

days.topic: Multiple Comparisons and False Discovery Rate
subtopics: Why many tests create false positives
days.lab_task: Test twenty customer segments for a treatment effect, show how many false positives appear without correction and compare Holm and Benjamini-Hochberg results.
checks: Uncorrected false positives are counted in simulated null data
Holm and Benjamini-Hochberg results are reported
The summary separates planned and exploratory findings

days.topic: Nonparametric Tests: Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon and Kruskal-Wallis
days.lab_task: Compare heavily skewed session durations between two app versions with a Mann-Whitney test, test before-and-after data with Wilcoxon and compare the results with t-tests.
checks: Nonparametric tests are chosen with reasons
Test results and effect sizes are reported
Differences from t-test results are explained

days.topic: Regression Diagnostics: Residuals, Leverage and Multicollinearity
days.lab_task: Diagnose a pricing regression with residual plots, Cook's distance and variance inflation factors, fix two problems and show how the conclusions change.
checks: Each diagnostic is run and interpreted
Two problems are fixed with transformations or robust errors

days.topic: Logistic Regression and Odds Ratios
subtopics: Model fit and pseudo R squared
days.lab_task: Model customer churn with logistic regression, interpret three odds ratios in plain words, plot predicted probabilities and choose a threshold for a retention campaign.
checks: The model is fitted and summarised
Odds ratios are explained in plain words
The threshold is chosen from campaign costs and benefits

days.topic: Generalised Linear Models: Poisson and Count Data
days.lab_task: Model weekly support tickets per customer with Poisson regression, test for overdispersion, refit with negative binomial and an exposure offset, and interpret rate ratios.
checks: Poisson and negative binomial models are fitted

days.topic: Penalised Regression for Many Predictors: Shrinkage, Selection and Tuning
days.lab_task: Fit ridge, lasso and elastic net models to predict customer value with fifty predictors, choose penalties by cross-validation and compare accuracy and selected variables.
checks: All three models are tuned by cross-validation
Accuracy and selected variables are compared
Limits of p-values after selection are stated

days.topic: Model Selection, Cross-Validation and Information Criteria
subtopics: Nested models and likelihood ratio tests
days.lab_task: Compare four candidate models with cross-validation and information criteria, find a leakage problem planted in the pipeline and choose and justify a final model.
checks: Models are compared with proper cross-validation
The planted leakage is found and fixed

days.topic: Bootstrap and Permutation Methods
days.lab_task: Bootstrap a confidence interval for the median order value and for a ratio metric, run a permutation test for a difference in medians and compare with formula-based results.
checks: Intervals for the median and ratio are reported
The permutation test result is reported
Differences from formula methods are explained

days.topic: Bayesian Inference with Priors and Posteriors
days.lab_task: Analyse an A/B test with a beta-binomial model, report the probability that the new version is better and the expected loss, and show how three priors change the result.
checks: Posteriors are computed for both variants
Probability of improvement and expected loss are reported

days.topic: Time Series Analysis: Trend, Seasonality and Autocorrelation
subtopics: Time series data and its structure
days.lab_task: Decompose two years of daily sales into trend and seasonality, test stationarity, read the autocorrelation plots and identify one structural break.
checks: Trend and seasonal parts are shown
Stationarity tests are run and interpreted
A structural break is identified with evidence

days.topic: Forecasting with ARIMA and Exponential Smoothing
subtopics: Error measures: MAE, RMSE and MAPE
days.lab_task: Forecast the next twelve weeks of sales with Holt-Winters and seasonal ARIMA, backtest both against a naive baseline and report forecasts with intervals.
checks: Both models are fitted and forecast
Backtest errors are compared with the naive baseline

days.topic: Survival Analysis: Kaplan-Meier and Cox Models
subtopics: Business uses: churn, failure and time to purchase
days.lab_task: Analyse time to customer churn with Kaplan-Meier curves by plan, compare plans with a log-rank test, fit a Cox model and interpret hazard ratios.
checks: The log-rank test result is reported
Hazard ratios are interpreted and assumptions checked

days.topic: Dimensionality Reduction: PCA and Factor Analysis
days.lab_task: Reduce thirty survey questions with PCA and factor analysis, choose the number of components, name the main factors and use them in a satisfaction model.
checks: The number of components is chosen with explained variance
Components are used in a model with results

days.topic: Handling Missing Data: Mechanisms and Imputation
subtopics: Missing completely at random, at random and not at random
Complete case analysis and its bias
Missing data in machine learning pipelines
Reporting how missing data were handled
days.lab_task: Explore missingness in a customer dataset, compare complete-case, mean imputation and multiple imputation for a regression and report how the estimates change.
checks: Three approaches are compared on the same model

days.topic: Causal Thinking: Confounding, Simpson's Paradox and Observational Data
days.lab_task: Analyse an observational dataset where a promotion appears to reduce sales, uncover the confounder behind Simpson's paradox and estimate an adjusted effect.
checks: The reversal is shown by group
Remaining limits of the causal claim are stated

days.topic: Statistics for Evaluating Machine Learning Models
subtopics: Confidence intervals for accuracy and AUC
days.lab_task: Compare two churn classifiers with bootstrap intervals for AUC and a McNemar test on the same test set, check calibration and report whether the difference is real.
checks: Metric intervals are reported for both models

days.topic: Reproducible Statistical Analysis: Notebooks, Scripts and Reports
days.lab_task: Turn an exploratory notebook into a reproducible project with pinned environment, seeds, a parameterised report and Git history, and have a peer reproduce the results.
checks: The environment is pinned and installs cleanly
A peer reproduces the same numbers
The parameterised report renders for two inputs

days.topic: Intermediate Capstone: Experiment Analysis and Recommendation
days.lab_task: Plan an experiment with a power analysis, analyse its results with integrity checks, guardrails and corrected segment results, and present a recommendation to a role-played product team.
checks: Power and analysis plan are fixed before results
Integrity, primary and guardrail results are reported
The recommendation follows from corrected results
objectives: Run an experiment analysis end to end

advanced.summary: For senior data scientists and analysts who own causal questions, experimentation and uncertainty for a business. Covers causal graphs, propensity scores, difference-in-differences and synthetic control, instrumental variables and regression discontinuity, hierarchical models, Bayesian modelling with PyMC and Stan, MCMC diagnostics, sequential testing, variance reduction, heterogeneous treatment effects, state space forecasting, probabilistic forecast evaluation, survey weighting, extreme values, conformal prediction, calibration, reproducibility, fairness measurement and running an experimentation platform.
prerequisites: Designs experiments and fits GLMs, survival and time series models
Comfortable with Python or R and probability
outcomes: Estimate causal effects from experiments and observational data with modern methods
Build and check Bayesian and hierarchical models
Run trustworthy experimentation with sequential testing, variance reduction and governance
Quantify uncertainty for forecasts and machine learning predictions and communicate it to leaders

days.topic: Causal Inference with Directed Acyclic Graphs
subtopics: Colliders and why not to adjust for them
days.lab_task: Draw a causal graph for the effect of a loyalty programme on spend with domain experts, find a valid adjustment set, estimate the effect with DoWhy and run refutation tests.
checks: The graph is agreed with a domain expert
The adjustment set blocks all back-door paths
Refutation tests are run and reported

days.topic: Propensity Scores, Matching and Weighting
tools: causal inference library such as DoWhy or EconML
days.lab_task: Estimate the effect of a training programme on employee retention with matching and weighting, check balance and overlap, and run a sensitivity analysis for hidden confounding.
days.deliverable: Propensity score analysis with sensitivity results
checks: Covariate balance improves after matching or weighting
Effects from two methods are compared

days.topic: Difference-in-Differences and Synthetic Control
subtopics: Before-and-after comparisons with a control group
days.lab_task: Estimate the effect of a regional price change with difference-in-differences and an event study, then with synthetic control, and run placebo tests.
days.deliverable: Two policy effect estimates with placebo tests
checks: Both methods give effect estimates with uncertainty

days.topic: Instrumental Variables and Regression Discontinuity
subtopics: Finding natural experiments in business data
days.lab_task: Estimate the effect of a free-shipping threshold on basket size with a regression discontinuity, and the effect of delivery speed on satisfaction with an instrument.
checks: The RDD estimate is reported with bandwidth checks

days.topic: Mixed-Effects and Hierarchical Models
subtopics: Grouped data: stores, schools and users
Hierarchical models for many small groups
days.lab_task: Model store sales with random intercepts and slopes by region, compare with separate and pooled models and show how partial pooling helps small stores.
checks: The mixed model converges and is summarised
Pooled, separate and mixed results are compared
Partial pooling for small stores is shown

days.topic: Bayesian Modelling with PyMC and Stan
subtopics: Stan and CmdStanPy as an alternative
days.lab_task: Build a hierarchical Bayesian model of conversion rates across fifty campaigns, run prior and posterior predictive checks and compare two models with LOO.
days.deliverable: Bayesian model with checks and comparison
checks: Priors are justified and checked with prior predictive draws

days.topic: MCMC Diagnostics and Model Checking
subtopics: How MCMC samplers work in brief
days.lab_task: Diagnose a poorly sampling hierarchical model, fix divergences with a non-centred parameterisation and report the diagnostics before and after.
checks: R-hat, effective sample size and divergences are reported

days.topic: Sequential Testing and Always-Valid Inference for Experiments
subtopics: Choosing a method for a platform
days.lab_task: Simulate the false positive rate from daily peeking, implement a group sequential design and a confidence sequence, and recommend a monitoring policy.
checks: Peeking inflates false positives in simulation
Both methods control error in simulation
The policy covers stopping for benefit and harm

days.topic: Variance Reduction in Experiments with CUPED
subtopics: Ratio metrics and the delta method
days.lab_task: Apply CUPED and regression adjustment to an experiment using pre-period spend, use the delta method for a ratio metric and report the reduction in required sample size.
checks: CUPED and regression adjustment estimates are reported
The delta method interval is reported
Variance and sample size reductions are stated

days.topic: Heterogeneous Treatment Effects and Uplift Modelling
subtopics: Meta-learners: S, T and X learners
days.lab_task: Estimate who responds most to a discount with meta-learners and a causal forest, evaluate with Qini curves and design a targeting rule with its expected gain.
checks: Conditional effects are estimated with two methods
The targeting rule states expected gain and risks

days.topic: State Space Models and Dynamic Forecasting
subtopics: Structural time series for causal impact
days.lab_task: Fit an unobserved components model to weekly demand with a promotion regressor, handle missing weeks and estimate the causal impact of a campaign.
days.deliverable: State space model and impact estimate
checks: The state space model is fitted and smoothed
Missing weeks are handled by the filter
The campaign impact is reported with intervals

days.topic: Forecast Evaluation and Probabilistic Forecasts
days.lab_task: Evaluate three forecasting methods with rolling-origin backtests on coverage, pinball loss and CRPS, reconcile store and region forecasts and report forecast value added.
checks: All three methods are scored on the same backtests
Interval coverage is compared with nominal levels
Reconciled forecasts are consistent across levels

days.topic: Survey Sampling, Weighting and Non-Response
tools: Python samplics or R survey package
days.lab_task: Weight a customer satisfaction survey to match population margins with raking, estimate satisfaction with correct standard errors and report the effective sample size.
checks: Effective sample size and non-response limits are stated

days.topic: Extreme Value Statistics and Anomaly Detection
subtopics: Block maxima and peaks over threshold
days.lab_task: Model extreme daily transaction values with peaks over threshold, estimate a one-in-a-hundred-days level, and build a seasonal control chart for anomalies with a target false alarm rate.
days.deliverable: Extreme value model and anomaly detector
checks: The tail model fit is checked
The return level is reported with uncertainty
The anomaly detector meets the false alarm target

days.topic: Conformal Prediction and Uncertainty for Machine Learning
subtopics: Conformal methods for time series in brief
days.lab_task: Add conformal prediction intervals to a house price model and prediction sets to a classifier, check coverage on held-out data and use the intervals in a pricing decision.
checks: Intervals and sets are produced for both models

days.topic: Model Calibration and Probability Scoring
days.lab_task: Check calibration of a credit risk model overall and by segment, recalibrate with isotonic regression and show the effect on expected loss decisions.
checks: Reliability diagrams and scores are reported
Expected loss decisions change as explained

days.topic: Reproducibility, p-Hacking and Pre-Registration
days.lab_task: Run a multiverse analysis of one question with twenty reasonable analysis choices, show how often the conclusion changes and write a pre-registration template for the team.
checks: The share of paths with each conclusion is reported
The template fixes key choices before data

days.topic: Statistics for Fairness and Bias Measurement
subtopics: Fairness questions in models and decisions
Uncertainty in fairness metrics for small groups
days.lab_task: Measure selection rates, error rates and calibration by group for a hiring screen model, add confidence intervals for small groups and write a fairness assessment.
checks: Group metrics are computed with intervals
The assessment states findings and limits

days.topic: Running an Experimentation Platform: Metrics, Guardrails and Governance
subtopics: Automated checks: sample ratio, novelty and carry-over
days.lab_task: Design the metric catalogue, automated checks, holdout policy and decision process for a company experimentation platform and present it to role-played product leaders.
checks: Each metric has a definition and owner
Integrity checks run for every experiment
Decision records and review rules are defined

days.topic: Advanced Capstone: Causal Impact Study for a Business Decision
days.lab_task: Answer a real causal question for a business, such as the effect of a pricing change, with a causal graph, two estimation methods, sensitivity analysis and an executive recommendation.
days.deliverable: Causal study, notebook and executive briefing
checks: The design and graph are justified
Two methods give consistent estimates or differences are explained
The recommendation states uncertainty and limits
